### Highlights

- Added a customizable global shortcut that opens a dedicated always-on-top host switcher, even when the main DisplayMux window is minimized or hidden.
- The host switcher supports mouse selection, Tab, Shift+Tab, Up and Down navigation, Enter to confirm, and Escape to close.
- Windows and macOS display Ctrl, Windows, Command, and Option keys according to each platform's conventions.

### Shortcut safety

- DisplayMux attempts to register a shortcut immediately after recording it to detect operating-system-level conflicts.
- The shortcut is checked again when settings are saved. If registration fails, the previous working shortcut remains active.
- Common application shortcuts such as Ctrl+W and Ctrl+S are rejected to avoid conflicts with browsers and other frequently used software.
- Windows shortcuts must include Ctrl, while macOS shortcuts must include Command. Additional modifiers are limited to reduce accidental activation.

### Release History improvements

- Fixed GitHub Release links in Help so they open correctly in the system browser.
- Release History now synchronizes published GitHub Releases automatically and displays the newest version first.
- Built-in release information remains available when GitHub cannot be reached.

### Compatibility

- Global shortcuts and the host switcher support Windows 10/11 and macOS 12 or later.
- Existing settings are migrated automatically. The global shortcut remains disabled by default until the user enables it.

### Known limitations

- Application-local shortcuts are not always registered as operating-system Global Hotkeys. DisplayMux blocks common combinations, but cannot maintain a complete list of shortcuts used internally by every third-party application.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed but not notarized with an Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper may require manual approval.
- Some MST, DisplayLink, and Silicon Motion docks do not forward DDC/CI. Software cannot restore control signals that the hardware does not expose.
